1. (Original) A method for generating a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules used to train a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a set of property measurements for a plurality of molecules, wherein each measurement assigns a value for a property of interest relative to a single molecule; selecting ordered tuples of molecules, from the plurality, wherein the molecules, in an ordered tuple of molecules, are ordered relative to one another and the property of interest; and combining the selected ordered tuples of molecules to form the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules.

2. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein selecting ordered tuples of molecules further comprises: applying at least a selection criteria to the plurality of molecules to determine which ordered tuples of molecules, from a set of all possible tuples of molecules, to include in the pseudo-partial ordering.

3. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the ordered tuples of molecules are assigned a weighting value.

4. (Original) The method of claim 2, wherein the selection criteria are selected from: determining whether a relative magnitude in the property measurements for the molecules, is above a selected threshold; determining whether an absolute difference in magnitude, in the property measurements for the molecules is above a selected threshold; and determining whether the probability that the measured values fall outside any experimental error intervals is above a selected threshold.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the ordered tuples of molecules used to form the pseudo-partial ordering contain two molecules, a first molecule and a second molecule.

6. (Original) The method of claim 5, wherein the property of interest assigns a discrete value indicating the presence, or absence, of the property of interest for a given molecule, and wherein the first molecule is assigned a discrete value indicating the presence of the property of interest for the first molecule, and the second molecule is assigned a discrete value indicating the absence of the property of interest for the second molecule.

7. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the molecules included in at least one ordered tuple of molecules represent the same physical molecule, and wherein the property of interest is measured relative to different substituent groups of the same physical molecule.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the molecules included in at least one ordered tuple of molecules represent different possible representations of the same physical molecule.

9. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein a molecule in an ordered tuple is selected from a plurality of virtual molecules, or wherein the ranked order for an ordered tuple is determined using virtual data.

10. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules is represented as a set of ordered pairs, ordered tuples, permutations or cross-products of molecules.

11. (Currently Amended) A method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm __on a computer__; providing the pseudo partial ordering of molecules to the selected machine learning algorithm __executing on the computer__; and __executing the selected machine learning algorithm on the computer using the pseudo partial ordering, thereby training a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model__.

12. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter, __wherein the predictions are generated by executing the trained molecular properties model on the computer__.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a classification learning algorithm __executed on the computer__.

14. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a kernel based learning algorithm.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof modified to process the pseudo partial ordering of ranked pairs, __wherein the algorithm is executed on the computer__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, an area above, or below, a receiver operator characteristic curve, __wherein the minimization is performed by executing the algorithm on the computer__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, a function of the rank ordering of molecules in the pseudo partial ordering, __wherein the minimization is performed by executing the algorithm on the computer__.

18. (Original) The method of claim 11, further comprising, determining an accuracy of the prediction for the additional molecule by carrying out laboratory experimentation using physically existing samples of the additional molecule, or by performing a research study using physical samples of the additional molecule.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules comprises: generating a vector representation of the molecules __on the computer__, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure of the molecules included the pseudo-partial ordering; or comprises generating an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering __on the computer__.

20. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein a threshold value or cutoff molecule is selected for the molecular proprieties model and used to create a classification model.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein the at least one additional molecule comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest, __wherein the ranking is generated by executing the trained molecular properties model on the computer__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are alternative representations of the same physical molecule and the property of interest is a property of the alternative representations, __wherein the training is performed on the computer__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are encoded to represent different atoms, bonds or substituent groups of the same molecule and the property of interest is a property of the atoms, bonds or substituent groups, __wherein the encoding and training are performed on the computer__.

35. (Currently Amended) A __non-transitory__ computer-storage medium containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; and generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm, wherein the pseudo partial ordering of molecules is provided to the selected machine learning algorithm, and wherein executing the selected machine learning algorithm, using the pseudo partial ordering, trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model.
